description: Negative Proposition N's registered counterexample (prereg/v3-core-reduct-correction.md), re-derived from first principles, not copied from the external review's own prose. Reachable set {(x=0,y=0),(x=1,y=1)}; the only two members differ in BOTH x and y simultaneously, so no reachable pair differs in exactly one property and the core (Definition 1's own participation criterion) is empty, even though M's verdict genuinely depends on the tuple: the empty set cannot distinguish (0,0) from (1,1). {x} and {y} are each independently sufficient and minimal -- reducts of cardinality 1 -- so the core (0) is strictly smaller than the minimum reduct (1) and is not itself a reduct.
verdict_field_note: M(x,y) is computed as bool(tuple[verdict_field]) -- a generic, formula-free way to encode 'M(x,y)=x' (equivalently '=y', since x and y are always equal on this reachable set) so checkers/core_insufficiency_counterexample.py evaluates it mechanically rather than re-deriving the formula from prose.
